title: Relative left lifting maps over small direct categories induce left lifting colimit maps
statement: Let $\mathcal B$ be a category admitting all small colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and let $T$ be any class of its morphisms. Write $\mathcal L={}^{\square}T$ for the maps with the left lifting property against every member of $T$, with the diagonal property as in [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure]. Let $K$ be any small category equipped with a function $e:\operatorname{Ob}K\to\mathbf N$ strictly increased by every nonidentity arrow; neither its objects nor its morphisms are required to be finite. For $D:K\to\mathcal B$, define $L_kD$ to be the colimit of the domain diagram on the full subcategory of $K/k$ obtained by deleting $1_k$, with commuting triangles as morphisms. For a natural transformation $f:A\to B$, the structure maps from the latching colimits to $A_k$ and $B_k$, together with $f_k$ and the induced map $L_kA\to L_kB$, define the relative latching map $\lambda_k(f):=A_k\amalg_{L_kA}L_kB\to B_k$. Suppose that every $\lambda_k(f)$ belongs to $\mathcal L$. Then the induced map $\operatorname{colim}_K A\to\operatorname{colim}_K B$ belongs to $\mathcal L$. The assertion includes the empty category. No factorization, weak equivalence, model structure or finiteness hypothesis is required.

source.place: Proposition 5.1.4 and Corollary 5.1.5, printed pp. 121-122: compatible lifts by increasing degree followed by the universal colimit cocone. Agent formulation for a single left lifting class, retaining arbitrary small direct categories; the source proof uses only lifting, not factorization. No Stacks tag states this direct-diagram lifting theorem. Stacks 002F (categories.tex, definition-colimit) supplies only its colimit notion.

proof.text: Use functional composition. Put $C_A=\operatorname{colim}_K A$, $C_B=\operatorname{colim}_K B$, with coprojections $a_k,b_k$, and let $F:C_A\to C_B$ be the map with $Fa_k=b_kf_k$. These equations define $F$ by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], since naturality of $f$ makes $(b_kf_k)$ a cocone. Fix any $p:X\to Y$ in $T$ and maps $u:C_A\to X$, $v:C_B\to Y$ with $pu=vF$. Set $u_k=ua_k$, $v_k=vb_k$. They are cocones and satisfy $pu_k=v_kf_k$. By the diagonal-property definition in [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure], it suffices to construct a cocone $h_k:B_k\to X$ with $h_kf_k=u_k$ and $ph_k=v_k$.

source.place: Corollary 5.1.5, printed pp. 121-122: the colimit square and its constant-diagram square; Stacks 002F, categories.tex, definition-colimit, for the cocone correspondence.

proof.text: Let $K_{<n}$ be the full subcategory of objects $k$ with $e(k)<n$. We construct compatible partial cocones $h^{(n)}$ on $B|_{K_{<n}}$, satisfying $h^{(n)}_kf_k=u_k$ and $ph^{(n)}_k=v_k$, and require that $h^{(n+1)}$ restricts to $h^{(n)}$. The base $n=0$ is the empty family. For an object $k$ of degree $n$, every object $\alpha:j\to k$ of its latching category has $e(j)<n$. A morphism from $\alpha:j\to k$ to $\beta:i\to k$ is $t:j\to i$ with $\beta t=\alpha$; both domains lie in $K_{<n}$. Thus $h^{(n)}_iB(t)=h^{(n)}_j$, so these components give a cocone on the entire latching diagram, including all its parallel arrows. Its index category is small, being a subcategory of $K/k$. The universal property in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives $\ell_k:L_kB\to X$ whose restriction on the coprojection indexed by $\alpha:j\to k$ is $h^{(n)}_j$.

source.place: Proposition 5.1.4, printed p. 121: induction on degree and the map out of the latching object. Natural-number degrees suffice for this item; the empty base and full partial-cocone invariant are explicit.

proof.text: Write $\iota^A_\alpha:A_j\to L_kA$, $\iota^B_\alpha:B_j\to L_kB$ for the latching coprojections, and $s^A_k:L_kA\to A_k$, $s^B_k:L_kB\to B_k$ for the latching structure maps. The map $L_kf:L_kA\to L_kB$ is defined by $L_kf\,\iota^A_\alpha=\iota^B_\alpha f_j$; compatibility follows from naturality of $f$. For every $\alpha:j\to k$ we have $\ell_kL_kf\,\iota^A_\alpha=h^{(n)}_jf_j=u_j=u_kA(\alpha)=u_ks^A_k\iota^A_\alpha$. Hence $\ell_kL_kf=u_ks^A_k$ by colimit uniqueness. The pushout $P_k=A_k\amalg_{L_kA}L_kB$, with coprojections $r_k:A_k\to P_k$, $s_k:L_kB\to P_k$, therefore gives $q_k:P_k\to X$ with $q_kr_k=u_k$ and $q_ks_k=\ell_k$. Naturality likewise gives $f_ks^A_k=s^B_kL_kf$, so its relative latching map $\lambda_k:P_k\to B_k$ satisfies $\lambda_kr_k=f_k$ and $\lambda_ks_k=s^B_k$. All these constructions and tests on coprojections use [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Proposition 5.1.4, printed p. 121: construction of the upper map from the relative latching pushout; Stacks 002F for both universal properties, expanded here.

proof.text: The square with left map $\lambda_k$, right map $p$, upper map $q_k$ and lower map $v_k$ commutes. On $A_k$ the equality $pq_k=v_k\lambda_k$ is $pu_k=v_kf_k$. On a latching component indexed by $\alpha:j\to k$, it is $p\ell_k\iota^B_\alpha=ph^{(n)}_j=v_j=v_kB(\alpha)=v_ks^B_k\iota^B_\alpha$; first latching-colimit and then pushout uniqueness [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] prove equality on $P_k$. By hypothesis $\lambda_k\in{}^{\square}T$ and the fixed map $p$ lies in $T$. The defining lifting property of [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure] supplies $h_k:B_k\to X$ with $h_k\lambda_k=q_k$ and $ph_k=v_k$. Its restrictions give $h_kf_k=u_k$ and $h_kB(\alpha)=h^{(n)}_j$ for every incoming nonidentity arrow $\alpha:j\to k$.

source.place: Proposition 5.1.4, printed p. 121, the relative latching lifting square. Only the defining diagonal property is used; no model-category axiom beyond the stated left lifting assumption is retained.

proof.text: Choose such a filler for each object of degree $n$, retaining all maps previously chosen on $K_{<n}$. This is a small family of independent choices of morphisms (ordinary classical choice). There is no nonidentity arrow between degree-$n$ objects, nor from a degree-$n$ object to an object of lower degree, by strict increase of $e$. Thus the last equation of Step 4 is exactly every new cocone equation, and identity arrows satisfy it automatically. It follows that these maps extend $h^{(n)}$ to $h^{(n+1)}$ with both required triangle equations. Iterate this operation by ordinary recursion on $n\in\mathbf N$. For each $k$ put $h_k=h^{(e(k)+1)}_k$. Restrictions agree at every later stage, so for any arrow $\alpha:j\to k$ the equation $h_kB(\alpha)=h_j$ is checked at stage $e(k)+1$; if $\alpha$ is nonidentity then $e(j)<e(k)$, and if it is identity the equation is tautological. We have therefore constructed the required cocone on all of $K$, even when degrees are unbounded or infinitely many objects have one degree.

source.place: Proposition 5.1.4, printed p. 121: independent choices at one degree and compatibility of the inductive lifts. Here the ordinal induction specializes to ordinary natural-number recursion, with no finiteness bound on the objects or arrows.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] the cocone $(h_k)$ gives $h:C_B\to X$ with $hb_k=h_k$. Then $hFa_k=h_kf_k=u_k=ua_k$ for every $k$, so $hF=u$ by uniqueness out of $C_A$. Likewise $phb_k=ph_k=v_k=vb_k$ for all $k$, so $ph=v$ by uniqueness out of $C_B$. This is a filler for the arbitrary square of Step 1. Since $p$ was arbitrary in $T$, [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure] identifies the conclusion as $F\in{}^{\square}T$. When $K$ is empty, the same argument uses empty cocones and uniqueness out of the two initial objects, so it still gives both equations. At an object with no nonidentity incoming arrow, $L_kA,L_kB$ are initial and Step 4 uses precisely the assumed relative latching map; it imposes no additional compatibility condition.

source.place: Corollary 5.1.5, printed pp. 121-122: descend the compatible lift through the colimit. Stacks 002F, categories.tex, definition-colimit, including the empty-colimit initial object.
